title: Signal Daily BIO — October 17, 2026
summary: 3 stories. RASONQUE’s positive EMA committee opinion adds a regulatory development alongside the CAR-T study and peptide-policy review. Other CAR-T and NAC/NAD+ records were single papers, trial-registry entries or lacked a second independent outlet.

stories.headline: Safety and Clinical Outcomes of a First-in-Human Trial of Point-of-Care Manufactured Trispecific CAR T Cells Targeting CD19, CD20, and CD22
stories.dek: A phase I study reported early clinical outcomes from a locally manufactured CAR T approach for relapsed or treatment-resistant B-cell cancers.
tldr: Researchers reported phase 1 results from a first-in-human, locally manufactured CAR T-cell approach targeting CD19, CD20 and CD22 in B-cell cancers.
The paper and Ohio State’s coverage say 18 people enrolled and 16 received treatment.
The early study is small and uncontrolled; longer follow-up is needed to assess durability, safety and reproducibility.

body.text: Researchers at Ohio State reported a first-in-human phase 1 study of trispecific CAR T cells for people with relapsed or treatment-resistant B-cell cancers. The cells were designed to target CD19, CD20 and CD22 and were manufactured at the treatment center.

The paper and Ohio State’s institutional coverage report that 18 participants enrolled and 16 received treatment. The multi-target design was intended to address the possibility that cancer cells could evade a therapy directed at a single target.
MedicalXpress summarized the work as an early clinical result. The study was small and did not compare the approach directly with standard treatment, so it cannot establish comparative benefit.

A larger cohort and longer follow-up are needed to assess how durable responses are, what adverse events occur and whether the local manufacturing process can be reproduced. These phase 1 findings are an early development signal, not evidence of an approved treatment or a recommendation for patients.

stories.whyItMatters: The study tests whether a multi-target design and local manufacturing can be advanced into clinical development. Its small, early-phase dataset leaves efficacy, long-term safety and reproducibility open.
stories.editorNote: Labels the findings as early phase 1 evidence and avoids implying comparative benefit or treatment advice.

stories.headline: Trump administration advances plan for peptide drugs favored by RFK Jr.
stories.dek: HHS sent an interim compounding policy for certain peptides to the White House for review; no rule or access change has been issued.
tldr: HHS submitted an interim policy concerning pharmacy compounding of certain peptides for White House review.
The Associated Press and The Epoch Times reported that the submission appeared in the federal review tracker; AP cited people familiar with a possible temporary enforcement-discretion approach.
The policy text has not been published and no final decision has been made, so current authorization or evidence of safety and efficacy has not changed.

body.text: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services submitted an “Interim Access Policy” concerning compounding of certain peptides to the White House Office of Management and Budget. The Associated Press and The Epoch Times reported that the submission appeared in the federal regulatory review tracker on October 14.

AP cited two people familiar with the plan who said it may include temporary enforcement discretion for compounding some peptides. The Epoch Times reported the title of the tracker entry but said the detailed policy text was not public.

Submission for review is an early administrative step, not FDA approval or a final rule. The available public record does not establish which substances would be covered or what conditions would apply.

This is a policy review concerning compounding and enforcement, rather than new clinical evidence about peptide therapies. Whether the proposal advances, which products it may cover and how safety concerns are addressed remain unresolved.

stories.whyItMatters: The development concerns a possible change in compounding policy, not a clinical finding. The proposal’s scope and final status are unknown, and no new evidence of safety or efficacy is reported.
stories.editorNote: Distinguishes the policy submission from FDA approval and from clinical evidence; detailed text remains unpublished.

stories.headline: EMA recommends approval of Revolution's pancreatic cancer drug
stories.dek: The EMA medicines committee recommended marketing authorization for RASONQUE (daraxonrasib); the European Commission still must decide.
tldr: The EMA committee recommended EU marketing authorization for Revolution Medicines’ RASONQUE (daraxonrasib).
The recommendation covers adults with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have received at least one prior systemic therapy.
A committee opinion is not final European Commission authorization, and the reports do not replace review of the full clinical evidence.

body.text: The European Medicines Agency’s medicines committee recommended marketing authorization for Revolution Medicines’ RASONQUE, also known as daraxonrasib. Reuters and Pharmaphorum reported the committee’s positive opinion on October 15.

The company says the proposed indication is for adults with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have received at least one prior systemic therapy. It said the recommendation followed review of the phase 3 RASolute 302 trial.

The milestone is a committee recommendation, not a final authorization. A European Commission decision is still required, and accessible news coverage does not provide a full independent appraisal of trial data.
The regulatory path and any eventual product information remain to be confirmed. The recommendation does not establish availability, reimbursement or outcomes outside the studied population.

stories.whyItMatters: The committee opinion is a step toward potential EU authorization for a late-stage pancreatic cancer therapy. The final regulatory decision and authorized indication remain pending.
stories.editorNote: Keeps the CHMP recommendation distinct from final European Commission authorization; no treatment advice.
